## The challenge

You will build a complete **k-nearest-neighbor image classifier** for CIFAR-10 without using a machine-learning implementation. The notebook gives you data loading, visualization, plotting, and small autograder helpers. You write the numerical and experimental core.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A[CIFAR-10 images] --> B[Broadcasted L2 distances]
    B --> C[k nearest labels]
    C --> D[Validation accuracy]
    D --> E[Choose k]
    E --> F[One final test]
```

This is the first part of a three-model sequence inspired by Stanford CS231n: **kNN**, a **linear Softmax classifier**, and a **linear SVM**. Each model will be implemented from scratch and evaluated under the same experimental discipline.

## What you implement

1. Pairwise squared L2 distances using NumPy broadcasting.
2. A `KNearestNeighbor` class whose `fit` method memorizes the training set.
3. Majority-vote prediction from the closest examples.
4. A reproducible train/validation split.
5. One validation experiment for a chosen value of `k`.

The notebook then provides the repeated cross-validation loop, uncertainty plot, final test evaluation, and nearest-neighbor visualization. You must interpret those results and justify your choice of `k`.

## Two-session rhythm

| Session | Work | Checkpoint |
|---|---|---|
| **A · Build the classifier** | inspect CIFAR-10, broadcasting, distance matrix, `fit`, nearest-neighbor voting | Checks 1–3 pass |
| **B · Choose rather than guess** | split data, run one validation experiment, cross-validation, choose `k`, inspect errors | Checks 4–5 pass; final plots and responses complete |

## Autograding

Every TODO is followed by an immediate check with tiny synthetic inputs, shape checks, edge cases, and comparison against a trusted reference. A green message means that the function satisfies the public contract.

:::{.callout-important}
Visible notebook checks support learning; they are not secure grading. The submitted notebook can later be evaluated with a separate instructor test file that imports the same functions and tests additional cases.
:::

## Submission standard

Restart the kernel and run the notebook from top to bottom. Submit the notebook with:

- all five checks passing;
- the cross-validation and final-test plots visible;
- a justified choice of `k` based only on validation evidence;
- at least three inspected successes or failures; and
- every reflection prompt answered in your own words.
